Under the payment clause [c6], escrow must be released upon acceptance, including deemed acceptance.
verdict.rationale: Clause [c3] establishes the required method of delivery, and the written record shows both required steps were completed. Clause [c2] confirms the delivery occurred on or before 10 September 2026. Clause [c4] is outcome-determinative because the client did not send a written defect notice within five business days, so the deliverable is deemed accepted. Clause [c6] then requires release of the escrowed sum upon acceptance, including deemed acceptance. The defendant’s strongest point is that the website was not on the production domain, but clause [c3] expressly places production deployment outside the contractor’s delivery obligation, so that objection does not defeat entitlement.

clauses.label: Scope
clauses.text:
The Contractor shall deliver a five-page responsive marketing website
   comprising Home, Product, Pricing, About and Contact pages, built to the
   wireframes attached as Schedule A.

clauses.label: Delivery date
clauses.text: The Contractor shall deliver on or before 10 September 2026.

clauses.label: Method of delivery
clauses.text:
Delivery is effected by (a) tagging the agreed release in
   the project Git repository, and (b) providing the Client with a working
   staging URL by email. Deployment to the Client's production domain is
   expressly outside the scope of this Agreement and is the Client's
   responsibility.

clauses.label: Acceptance notice period
clauses.text:
The Client shall have five (5) business days from delivery to
   notify the Contractor in writing of any defect. Absent written notice of
   defect within that period, the deliverable is deemed accepted.

clauses.label: Revisions
clauses.text:
Two rounds of revisions are included, provided they are requested
   within the acceptance period defined in clause 4.

clauses.label: Payment upon acceptance
clauses.text:
The escrowed sum shall be released to the Contractor upon
   acceptance, whether express or deemed under clause 4.

clauses.label: Disputes
clauses.text:
Any dispute as to whether delivery or acceptance occurred shall be
   determined by reference to the written record of the parties.

claim.summary: The parties dispute whether the website was delivered in the contractually required manner on 8 September 2026 and, if so, whether the absence of a written defect notice within the acceptance period resulted in deemed acceptance and release of escrow.

findings.plaintiff_position: The contractor says the release tagged v1.0-delivery covered all five Schedule A pages, and the staging report shows HTTP 200 responses for Home, Product, Pricing, About, and Contact.
findings.defendant_position: The client says nothing in the record shows the website was delivered as required on the client’s own domain, and that the site was not visible there.
findings.rationale: The clause requires a five-page responsive marketing website comprising the listed pages, built to the wireframes. The contractor’s tag, delivery email, and uptime report together show all five required pages were present on the staging site and that the release was tagged as delivery. The defendant’s materials focus on the production domain, which clause 3 expressly excludes from the delivery method and therefore does not negate the scope showing in the record.

findings.plaintiff_position: The contractor’s evidence shows the tagged delivery occurred on 8 September 2026, before the 10 September 2026 deadline.
findings.defendant_position: The client says the site was never delivered, so the deadline was not met.
findings.rationale: The record shows a delivery tag dated 2026-09-08 and a delivery email sent the same day. That is on or before 10 September 2026. The defendant’s contrary position is not supported by evidence showing a later or missing delivery under the contract’s delivery method.

findings.plaintiff_position: The contractor says delivery was effected by tagging v1.0-delivery in the repo and providing a working staging URL by email; production deployment was the client’s responsibility.
findings.defendant_position: The client says the site was not on the production domain and expected it there, but also acknowledges not reading clause 3 closely.
findings.rationale: Clause 3 requires two things: a tagged release in the repository and a working staging URL by email. The contractor’s tag log and delivery email satisfy both, and the staging report corroborates that the URL worked. The defendant’s evidence concerns the production domain, which the clause expressly places outside the contractor’s delivery obligation.

findings.plaintiff_position: The contractor says the delivery email on 8 September 2026 triggered a five-business-day defect window, and no timely written defect notice is shown within that period.
findings.defendant_position: The client’s 16 September email says the site was never delivered and refuses escrow, but it does not identify a defect in writing within five business days of delivery.
findings.rationale: Using the 8 September 2026 delivery date, five business days excluding weekends are 9 Sep, 10 Sep, 11 Sep, 12 Sep, and 15 Sep 2026. The defendant’s email is dated 16 Sep 2026, which is outside that period. The record contains no earlier written defect notice. Accordingly, the deliverable is deemed accepted under the clause.

findings.plaintiff_position: The contractor states two revision rounds are included if requested within the acceptance window.
findings.defendant_position: The client’s email does not request revisions; it disputes delivery and escrow instead.
findings.rationale: The clause makes revisions available only if requested within the acceptance period. The record shows the acceptance period ran from 8 September through 15 September 2026, and no revision request appears within that window. Because the clause is conditional and the condition was not invoked, the contractor’s inclusion of two rounds stands unbreached on this record.

findings.plaintiff_position: The contractor says escrow should be released once acceptance occurs, including deemed acceptance.
findings.defendant_position: The client says escrow should not be released because the site was never delivered and he cannot see it on the production domain.
findings.rationale: Clause 6 requires release upon acceptance, express or deemed under clause 4. Clause 4 is satisfied by deemed acceptance because no timely written defect notice appears in the record. Therefore the escrow release obligation is triggered.

findings.plaintiff_position: The contractor relies on the written record showing tagged delivery, a working staging URL, and no timely defect notice.
findings.defendant_position: The client relies on the written record showing the production domain was empty and that he believed the site was never delivered.
findings.rationale: This clause directs disputes to be determined by the written record, and the record here contains competing evidence on delivery and acceptance. The record is sufficient to decide the specific delivery-method and acceptance clauses above, but clause 7 itself does not create an additional factual breach or compliance event beyond that dispute-resolution instruction. On its own terms, the clause is not separately shown to be complied with or violated.
